mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime that raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If, during periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 5% for two consecutive months, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST monthly change < -10%
failure_condition: If, during such episodes, the S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of cases, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which pressure corporate margins and reduce earnings growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If, in more than 50% of such periods, the 20-day forward returns are positive, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its prior 12-month average for four consecutive months signals broad-based supply chain weakness, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of such episodes, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate below 3% combined with a concurrent decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below 2% signals a deflationary easing cycle, which boosts risk appetite and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 3.0% AND CPIAUCSL < 102 (i.e., <2% YoY) in the same month
failure_condition: If, in more than 60% of such triggered months, the 20-day forward returns are negative, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A strong acceleration in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth > 0.5% month-over-month) with a concurrent rise in housing starts (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average signals robust demand expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS month-over-month change > 0.5% AND HOUST > 12-month moving average
failure_condition: If, in more than 60% of such triggered months, the 20-day forward returns are negative, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for five consecutive months signals a tight labor market that boosts wage inflation and input costs, which ultimately pressures margins and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If, in more than 50% of such periods, the 60-day forward returns are positive, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent year-over-year decline in real personal savings (proxied by RSAFS) below its 5-year average, combined with a concurrent drop in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1), signals weakening household balance sheets and reduced consumption capacity, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 5-year average for three consecutive months AND GDPC1 YoY change < 0%
failure_condition: If, in more than 55% of such triggered quarters, the 60-day forward returns are positive, the hypothesis is rejected.
